questions.stem: The correct order of acid strength of the following carboxylic acids is
questions.solution: The carboxylate is stabilised most when the carboxyl carbon is attached to an electron-withdrawing sp carbon, so propiolic acid (I) is the strongest. The sp² vinyl carbon of acrylic acid (II) withdraws less. In p-methoxybenzoic acid (III) the OMe group donates electrons by resonance and weakens the acid, but it remains stronger than propanoic acid (IV), whose sp³ ethyl group donates electrons inductively. Order: I > II > III > IV.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: Which of the following statement(s) is(are) true?

options.text: Monosaccharides cannot be hydrolysed to give polyhydroxy aldehydes and ketones
Oxidation of glucose with bromine water gives glutamic acid
Hydrolysis of sucrose gives dextrorotatory glucose and laevorotatory fructose
The two six-membered cyclic hemiacetal forms of D-(+)-glucose are called anomers

questions.solution: Monosaccharides are the simplest sugars and cannot be hydrolysed further, so (A) is true. Bromine water oxidises only the CHO group of glucose, giving gluconic acid; glutamic acid is an amino acid, so (B) is false. Hydrolysis of sucrose gives D-(+)-glucose and D-(−)-fructose, i.e. a dextrorotatory and a laevorotatory sugar, so (C) is true. The α and β pyranose forms of D-glucose differ only at C1 and are called anomers, so (D) is true.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Choose the correct option(s) for the following set of reactions
C₆H₁₀O —i) MeMgBr ii) H₂O→ Q —conc. HCl→ S (major)
Q —20% H₃PO₄, 360 K→ R (major)
R —i) H₂, Ni ii) Br₂, hν→ T (major)
R —HBr, benzoyl peroxide, Δ→ U (major)
questions.solution: C₆H₁₀O is cyclohexanone; MeMgBr gives 1-methylcyclohexanol (Q). Conc. HCl substitutes through the tertiary cation, so S is 1-chloro-1-methylcyclohexane. Dehydration gives the more substituted alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene (R). Hydrogenation gives methylcyclohexane, and radical bromination picks the tertiary C–H, so T is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane. HBr with peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov, so U is 1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane. Options C and D list correct pairs.

questions.stem:
Schemes 1 and 2 describe the conversion of P to Q and R to S, respectively. Scheme 3 describes the synthesis of T from Q and S. The total number of Br atoms in a molecule of T is ______
Scheme 1: P —i) Br₂ (excess), H₂O ii) NaNO₂, HCl, 273 K iii) CuCN/KCN iv) H₃O⁺, Δ v) SOCl₂, pyridine→ Q (major)
Scheme 2: R —i) Oleum ii) NaOH, Δ iii) H⁺ iv) Br₂, CS₂, 273 K→ S (major)
Scheme 3: S —i) NaOH ii) Q→ T (major)
questions.solution: Bromine water converts aniline into 2,4,6-tribromoaniline; diazotisation, Sandmeyer cyanation and hydrolysis give 2,4,6-tribromobenzoic acid, and SOCl₂ gives the acid chloride Q (3 Br). Benzene is sulfonated, fused with NaOH and acidified to give phenol, which with Br₂ in CS₂ at low temperature is monobrominated at the para position, so S is 4-bromophenol (1 Br). The phenoxide of S is acylated by Q to give 4-bromophenyl 2,4,6-tribromobenzoate, with 4 Br atoms.
